prop:toroidal-harmonics-delta-lambda:
Proposition A toroidal-harmonic change of variables and the Markov loop values.

Toroidal Harmonics and the \Delta_\lambda Mass Gap

Bridging the mass calculation from the canonical base m_{\text{can}} to the AME2020 experimental frontier requires resolving the \Delta_\lambda normalization shift (the shell-filling fraction c_\lambda).

The toroidal change of variables

The toroidal Legendre equation of half-integer degree n - \tfrac12,

(1 - x^2)\, y'' - 2x\, y' + \left(n^2 - \tfrac14\right) y = 0,

is carried by the substitution x = \frac{1}{2w} - 1 (equivalently w = \frac{1}{2(x+1)}), after multiplication by 4, exactly onto the second-order equation

4w^2(4w - 1)\, f'' + 16 w^2 f' + (4n^2 - 1) f = 0 .

This is a change of variables and holds for every choice of what w is later identified with; it is independent of any Markov-trace convention.

Identifying w with a Markov loop value

Write q = e^{\eta}, so \eta = \ln q and [2]_q = q + q^{-1} = 2\cosh\eta. The canonical Markov parameter is

z(q) = \frac{q^3}{q^2 + 1} = \frac{q^2}{[2]_q} = \frac{e^{2\eta}}{2\cosh\eta},

and the negative loop value is z_-(q) = z(q) - (q - q^{-1}) = \frac{1}{q(q^2+1)}. The bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} exchanges them, z(q^{-1}) = z_-(q), so z itself is not a function of \cosh\eta and w = z^2 does not satisfy \frac{1}{2w} - 1 = \cosh\eta. At the aether modulus q_0 \approx 1.10998 one has z^2 \approx 0.375387, against \frac{1}{2(\cosh\eta_0 + 1)} \approx 0.249321; the corresponding x = \frac{1}{2z^2} - 1 \approx 0.331960 is less than 1, so it is not \cosh of any real angle. The identification w = z^2 therefore has no toroidal reading.

The bar-invariant combination of the two loop values does have one:

w = z\, z_- = \frac{1}{[2]_q^{\,2}} = \frac{1}{2(\cosh 2\eta + 1)}, \qquad x = \frac{1}{2w} - 1 = \cosh 2\eta .

So under the canonical weight the toroidal coordinate is \cosh 2\eta, the full angle of q, rather than a half angle. At q_0: \eta_0 = \ln q_0 \approx 0.104341, w = z z_- \approx 0.247298, and x = \cosh 2\eta_0 \approx 1.021853.

prf:q-bessel-c-k-recurrence-cfinite:
Proof Throughout, q and the order \nu are formal parameters in a field; no archimedean structure is used. Write (x;q)_k = \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1 - x q^{j}\bigr) for the q-Pochhammer symbol, with (x;q)_0 = 1.

Step 1 — the closed-form coefficients and their ratio. The Hahn–Exton q-Bessel function of order \nu has power-series coefficients

c_k \;=\; \frac{(-1)^k\, q^{k(k-1)/2}}{(q;q)_k\,\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_k}, \qquad k \ge 0 .

Compare consecutive coefficients. The sign contributes a factor -1; the Gaussian exponent contributes q^{k(k+1)/2 - k(k-1)/2} = q^{k}; and each q-Pochhammer symbol gains exactly one factor,

\frac{(q;q)_{k+1}}{(q;q)_k} = 1 - q^{k+1},
\qquad
\frac{\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_{k+1}}{\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_k} = 1 - q^{\nu+k+1}.

Multiplying out, the coefficients satisfy the first-order q-recurrence

c_{k+1}\,\bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr) \;=\; -\,q^{k}\, c_k
\qquad (\star)

for all k \ge 0.

Step 2 — first-order recurrences integrate to a product. Conversely, (\star) determines the sequence from its seed. Let (r_k)_{k \ge 0} be any sequence of scalars and suppose a sequence (c_k) satisfies c_{k+1} = r_k\, c_k for all k. Then, by induction on k,

c_k \;=\; c_0 \prod_{j=0}^{k-1} r_j ,

the empty product being 1 at k = 0 and the induction step reading c_{k+1} = r_k\, c_k = c_0 \prod_{j=0}^{k} r_j. For generic parameters the denominators \bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr) never vanish (vanishing requires q a root of unity or q^{\nu+1} \in q^{-\mathbb{N}}), so (\star) is of this form with ratio

r_k \;=\; \frac{-\,q^{k}}{\bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr)} ,

and every solution of (\star) is the q-hypergeometric product c_k = c_0 \prod_{j=0}^{k-1} r_j. In particular the closed form of Step 1 is the unique solution with c_0 = 1.

Step 3 — q-holonomic, with C-finite as the degeneration. The ratio r_k depends on k through q^{k}: the recurrence (\star) is first-order linear with q^{k}-dependent coefficients, so the sequence (c_k) is q-holonomic. A constant-coefficient (C-finite) recurrence arises exactly in the degenerate case of a k-independent ratio: if c_{k+1} = \rho\, c_k for a single scalar \rho, the product of Step 2 collapses to the geometric sequence

c_k = c_0\, \rho^{k},

which is C-finite of order 1 with characteristic root \rho. This degeneration occurs in the rational limit of the underlying q-difference kernel (in particular after the q \to 1 contraction, where the rescaled ratio (1-q)^2\, c_{k+1}/c_k tends to -1/\bigl((k+1)(\nu+k+1)\bigr), the coefficient ratio of the classical Bessel series), never for the genuine q-Bessel ratio r_k.

Step 4 — consequence for the precision-ladder coefficients. At the fibre level the ladder kernel is a q-Bessel object, not a rational function; by Step 3 its coefficient sequence therefore admits no low-order constant-coefficient recurrence, while the dominant-root structure of the associated q-difference kernel survives. The canonical ladder values c_2, \ldots, c_{10}, expanded in the ladder variable u \approx 0.00852, exhibit exactly this pair of signatures: no constant-coefficient recurrence of order at most 4 fits them, while the tail ratio approaches the reciprocal pole location, c_{k+1}/c_k \to 1/u \approx 117.4. \blacksquare

prf:q-bessel-second-order-qdifference:
Proof Throughout, q and the order \nu are formal parameters in a field; the argument is purely q-difference-algebraic. Write (x;q)_k = \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1 - x q^{j}\bigr) for the q-Pochhammer symbol, and let

g(w) \;=\; \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k\, w^{k},
\qquad
c_k \;=\; \frac{(-1)^k\, q^{k(k-1)/2}}{(q;q)_k\,\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_k},

be the generating function of the Hahn–Exton q-Bessel coefficients of order \nu. By the contiguity recurrence, the coefficients satisfy the first-order relation

c_k\,\bigl(1 - q^{k}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k}\bigr) \;=\; -\,q^{k-1}\, c_{k-1},
\qquad k \ge 1. \qquad (\star)

Step 1 — assemble the three q-shifts. The q-shifted series are g(qw) = \sum_{k} c_k\, q^{k} w^{k} and g(q^2 w) = \sum_{k} c_k\, q^{2k} w^{k}. Hence

q^{\nu}\, g(q^2 w) - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu}\bigr)\, g(q w) + g(w)
\;=\; \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k \Bigl( q^{\nu+2k} - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu}\bigr) q^{k} + 1 \Bigr) w^{k},

and the bracket factors,

q^{\nu+2k} - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu}\bigr) q^{k} + 1
\;=\; \bigl(1 - q^{k}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k}\bigr),

as one checks by expanding the right-hand side. This factorisation into the (\star) denominator is the reason the second-order operator collapses onto the first-order recurrence.

Step 2 — the source term. Re-indexing a single q-shift multiplied by w,

w\, g(q w) \;=\; \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k\, q^{k} w^{k+1} \;=\; \sum_{k \ge 1} c_{k-1}\, q^{k-1} w^{k}.

Step 3 — coefficient comparison. Combining Steps 1 and 2, the w^{k} coefficient of

q^{\nu}\, g(q^2 w) - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu} - w\bigr)\, g(q w) + g(w)

is c_0 \bigl(1 - q^{0}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu}\bigr) = 0 for k = 0, and

c_k\,\bigl(1 - q^{k}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k}\bigr) + q^{k-1}\, c_{k-1}

for k \ge 1. By (\star) every coefficient vanishes, so the generating function satisfies the second-order q-difference equation

q^{\nu}\, g(q^2 w) \;-\; \bigl(1 + q^{\nu} - w\bigr)\, g(q w) \;+\; g(w) \;=\; 0.
\qquad (\star\star)

Writing \eta for the q-shift operator (\eta f)(w) = f(qw), equation (\star\star) reads \bigl[\,q^{\nu}\eta^{2} - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu} - w\bigr)\eta + 1\,\bigr] g = 0: a genuine second-order (three-point: w, qw, q^2 w) q-difference operator, whose linear term +w in the middle coefficient is the source making the coefficient ladder descend.

Step 4 — equivalence of (\star\star) and (\star). The computation in Steps 1–3 is reversible: (\star\star) holds if and only if every w^{k} coefficient vanishes, and for k \ge 1 that vanishing is exactly (\star). The "second order" refers to the q-difference order (three q-shifted arguments); on the coefficients the equation collapses to a two-term relation between consecutive c_k, precisely because the middle coefficient factors through the (\star) denominator as in Step 1. Equivalently, shifting the index to k+1, the coefficient relation is

\Bigl( q^{\nu+2k+2} - q^{k+1} - q^{\nu+k+1} + 1 \Bigr) c_{k+1} + q^{k}\, c_k = 0,
\qquad
q^{\nu+2k+2} - q^{k+1} - q^{\nu+k+1} + 1 = \bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr).

Step 5 — classical contraction. In the limit q \to 1^{-} the rescaled operator contracts to the ordinary Bessel operator w\, g'' + (\nu + 1)\, g' + g acting on g(w): the denominators degenerate as 1 - q^{k} \sim k\,(1-q) and 1 - q^{\nu+k} \sim (\nu+k)(1-q), so the rescaled coefficient ratio satisfies \lim_{q \to 1^{-}} (1-q)^{2}\, c_k / c_{k-1} = -1/\bigl(k(\nu+k)\bigr), the coefficient recurrence of the classical Bessel series \sum_{k} (-1)^k z^k / \bigl(k!\, (\nu+1)_k\bigr) in a formal variable z, where (\nu+1)_k is the ordinary Pochhammer symbol. \blacksquare

     {\prod_{k\ge 0}\bigl(1 + e^{-i\pi b^{-2}(2k+1)}\,e^{2\pi z/b}\bigr)},

which on the branch \mathrm{Im} b^2 > 0 converges and equals the Faddeev contour integral. It is the canonical solution — it satisfies both hypotheses with c = 1, so the admissible class is nonempty and the constant is genuinely pinned.

The two first-order q-difference equations are invariant under multiplication by any function elliptic for the aether lattice \langle ib, i/b\rangle: the shift multipliers cancel in the ratio \Phi_1/\Phi_b, which is therefore doubly periodic. A nonconstant elliptic factor — a full-lattice Weierstrass \wp — is thus compatible with the difference equations and would give a second, non-proportional solution.   1. The inversion relation \Phi_b(x)\Phi_b(-x) = c_0 excludes the even part of the elliptic freedom algebraically.
  2. \sigma-unitarity (self-duality, \lvert\Phi_b\rvert = 1) excludes the bar-even reciprocal-odd part algebraically.

Standing

Every analytic ingredient is established without contour integration. The product \Phi_b is meromorphic on the branch (its two infinite products are entire, as locally-uniform limits of entire partial products), its zeros are isolated (each factor's zeros form a discrete lattice, and the products vanish only where a factor does), and the strip growth follows from elementary product-norm bounds.   1. Ratio test. c_{k+1}/c_k \to r_{\max} = 1/\rho.

rem:q-beta-direction-sanity-gate-argumen:
Remark Argument for q beta direction sanity gate (not a proof).

Proof

Write q_0 for the aether modulus, u = b(q)\,\hbar_q^2 for the ladder variable of the precision-ladder factorisation

\mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q)
= Q_A(q)\cdot\cos\bigl(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q)\bigr)
  \cdot\prod_{k \ge 2}\bigl(1 + c_k\,u^k\bigr)

(c_2 structural identity), u_0 \approx 8.517\times 10^{-3} for its aether value, and c_k for the pinned ladder coefficients. A candidate Habiro element F(q) is a proposed closed form for the correction factor \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q)/[Q_A(q)\cos(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q))] (c_k recursion), and the target magnitude is

F_{\text{target}}(q_0)
:= \frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{CODATA}}}
        {Q_A(q_0)\cdot\cos\bigl(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q_0)\bigr)}
\approx 0.998 .

The gate. F passes when F_{\text{target}}(q_0)/10 \le |F(q_0)| \le 10\,F_{\text{target}}(q_0) (same order of magnitude, one decade each way) and is screened out otherwise. The additive test |F(q_0) - F_{\text{target}}(q_0)|/F_{\text{target}}(q_0) > 10 is not a sufficient condition for failure when F(q_0) may be negative: F_{\text{target}}=1, F(q_0)=-19/2 passes the window but fails the additive test. For F(q_0)\ge0 it is sufficient, but it never rejects a too-small magnitude (The order-of-magnitude screen \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x), item 6).

Step 1 — the target has order of magnitude one. Every ladder factor satisfies |c_k u_0^k| \le |c_2|\,u_0^2 \approx 7.3\times 10^{-5}, with the sequence |c_k|\,u_0^k decreasing to the flat asymptote \approx 2.1\times 10^{-13} measured on the window c_2, \ldots, c_{10} (radius-of-convergence gate computation). Hence

\Bigl\lvert \ln \prod_{k \ge 2}\bigl(1 + c_k u_0^k\bigr) \Bigr\rvert
\;\le\; 2\sum_{k \ge 2} |c_k|\,u_0^k
\;\lesssim\; 2\times 10^{-4}
\;\ll\; \ln 10 ,

so the correction product lies within a factor e^{\pm 2\times 10^{-4}} of unity: it cannot move the base value Q_A \cos\alpha_{\text{eff}} by even a fraction of a decade. The empirical target evaluates to F_{\text{target}}(q_0) \approx 0.998 (gate witness), consistent with this bound. Order-of-magnitude proximity to the target is therefore an invariant that every faithful candidate for the correction factor must satisfy.

Step 2 — soundness of rejection. F_{\text{target}}(q_0) > 0, and the true kernel — the element whose expansion generates the canonical c_k — evaluates at q_0 to the correction product of Step 1, hence within 2\times 10^{-4} (in log) of order unity and, up to the sub-percent accuracy of the ladder itself (negligible at a decade threshold), to F_{\text{target}}(q_0). Its window ratio is \approx 1 \ll 10: granted that ladder comparison, the true kernel passes at any decade threshold, so the screen raises no false refutation. Contrapositively, if the true kernel passes, a candidate whose magnitude falls outside the decade window has F(q_0) \ne F_{\text{true}}(q_0) (The order-of-magnitude screen \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x), item 2). That premise rests on the comparison of the ladder with \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{CODATA}} and on the infinite ladder bound, whose convergence is not proved, so rejection is conditional, not definitive. Passage is only necessary — a passing candidate still faces the exact \S 4(c) integer shadows and the \S 4(a) pole-location test, which is conditional on the radius-of-convergence conjecture.

Step 3 — calibration of the 10\times threshold. Two constraints bound the admissible threshold window.

  1. Lower bound. The gate must not refute legitimate fibre-level candidates whose archimedean evaluations swing between anchor pins: recorded cross-anchor swings reach \approx 3.5\,\% at the c_3 level, while the aether variable itself shifts by only 2.1\times 10^{-7} (210 ppb) under the proton–muon re-pin, moving the target through the ladder by \bigl(\sum_k k\,|c_k|\,u_0^k\bigr)\cdot 2.1\times 10^{-7} \approx 3\times 10^{-11} in log — utterly negligible. Any threshold well above the few-percent near-match band therefore tests direction, not anchor choice or near-match precision.
  2. Upper bound. The threshold must still catch the geometric-decay direction errors of Step 4, which for m \ge 5 escape only thresholds \gtrsim 11.6.

The decade convention 10\times sits inside this admissible window. Finer discrimination is deliberately delegated to the complementary gates, which admit no tolerance at all (\S 4(c)) or a 10^{-6} fibre-level tolerance (\S 4(a)).

Step 4 — non-vacuity: the stabilisation direction obstruction. The canonical refuted precedent is the family of trace-level candidates whose aether magnitude is a power of the positive-stabilisation weight, at the canonical value z = q^3/(q^2+1). This satisfies z < 1 exactly when q^3 - q^2 - 1 < 0, that is for 1 < q < \psi \approx 1.4656 (the real root of x^3 = x^2 + 1); the aether lies in that range, with z(q_0) \approx 0.6127. A candidate with |F(q_0)| = z(q_0)^m after m stabilisations therefore satisfies

\frac{F_{\text{target}}(q_0)}{|F(q_0)|}
\;\approx\; 0.998 \cdot 1.632^{\,m},

which, at the retired z = 1 base target \approx 0.998, exceeds 10 first at m = 5 (where it is \approx 11.6; at m = 4 it is \approx 7.1). The first rejected m depends on the target: it is m = 4 at the z = q^3/(q^2+1) target \approx 1.76. Repeated stabilisation can only shrink the magnitude — it can never climb to a target of order unity, let alone to the linking-weight scale \approx 2.5 of the precedent — and, at that target, the gate screens out every member with m \ge 5 (The order-of-magnitude screen \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x), item 5). The members with m \le 4 are not caught by the decade threshold; their exclusion rests on the direction argument itself, not on this gate. \blacksquare
